resources.string: The saved camera calibration is deleted; the camera falls back to its own estimate.
The saved laser calibration is deleted, with the lines collected toward a new one.
The measured board shape is deleted and measured again from the next views.
The points scanned so far are deleted.
Point the phone at the ChArUco board: the overlay shows the pose and its error.
Calibrate the camera: Start, then move and tilt the phone slowly around the board, so the board visits every part of the frame. It saves on its own.
Calibrate the laser plane: Start, then sweep the stripe across the board at varied tilts.
Start, then sweep the laser over the object. Export writes the cloud as a PLY to Download/EasyScanner.
The viewfinder: the overlay shows the board pose and its fit. Long-press the board status for the debug overlay with every number.

Start collects steady views of the board; Pause keeps them. The solve runs once the target is reached and the board was seen tilted from every side. A rejected solve stops with its reason: add views, or start over.\n\nCapture adds the current view by hand. Forget K deletes the saved calibration.
Start collects laser lines on the board; Pause keeps them. The plane is fitted and saved on its own once the lines are varied enough. Force fit saves it with the lines so far.

Export writes a Z-up PLY over the board (mm) to Download/EasyScanner and offers to share it.\n\nStart photos (in the overflow menu) takes posed full-resolution keyframes into a photogrammetry session; stopping it adds laser.ply.
Could not copy the scan to Downloads; it stays in the app\'s files.
This camera offers no photo size with the analysis aspect.
The scanner sees the board and the laser through the camera, so it cannot work without it. Allow the camera in the app\'s settings (Permissions › Camera), then come back.
Another app took the camera. The scanner goes on when it is free again.
Lay the printed board flat and point the phone at it.

The app has to know which board you printed: its size, squares and markers are printed on the sheet. When the board is in view, the grid drawn over the picture must lie exactly on the printed squares. If it does not, or the app reports a wrong board, pick the board you printed.\n\nThe board does not have to lie perfectly flat: while you move the phone, the app measures its shape and corrects for it.
Board shape: taken as flat until measured
Board shape: measured, %1$.1f mm off flat
The board was moved, so its shape was measured again.
Markers seen, but they do not fit this board: pick the board you printed.
Hold the phone as far from the board as you will scan from, and wait until the picture is sharp.

A camera calibration only holds at the focus it was taken at, so the focus is locked for calibrating and scanning. Hold the phone about as far from the board as you will be from the object, wait until the picture is sharp, then lock it.\n\nIf the camera was calibrated before, \"Use calibrated focus\" goes back to that focus and keeps the calibration.
Move the phone slowly around the board, tilted to every side, near and far.

The calibration measures the lens. Press Start, then move the phone slowly around the board: tilt it 30–45° to every side, near and far, so the board visits every part of the picture. It saves on its own when it has enough views.
Enough views, but still too few tilted ones. Tilt the phone about 30° so it looks at the board from %1$s.
Not saved: too few views showed enough of the board.
Not saved: the views do not agree. Blurred views, or the board in Settings is not the printed one.
Not saved: the result is not a plausible camera.
Not saved: the views do not pin down the focal length. More tilted views help, also closer to the board.
Add views to try again, or start over.
The set is full: start over.
Laser on, board empty. Sweep the stripe across the board, and change the tilt between sweeps.

This finds where the laser line lies relative to the camera. Switch the laser on and clear the board. Press Start, then sweep the stripe across the board, changing the phone\'s tilt between sweeps. It saves on its own; \"Force fit\" saves early with the lines so far.
The saved laser calibration belongs to an earlier camera calibration: calibrate the laser again.
Put the object on the board, sweep the laser over it and walk slowly around it. Keep the board in view.
Hold still now and then for a photo.

Press Start, then sweep the laser line over the object while you walk slowly around it; the board must stay in the picture. Pause stops collecting points, Finish saves the scan to Download/EasyScanner.\n\nWith photos on, the app takes a sharp photo whenever you hold still for a moment; together with the points they make a session for photogrammetry.
photo due: board out of view
The scan stopped: the point cloud is full. Finish the scan to save it.
The scan stopped: the board was moved. The points so far belong to its old position: export or clear them before scanning on.
The scan is still open. Finish saves it to Download/EasyScanner; Discard deletes it.
Its points and photos are deleted from the phone.
Board not found: keep all of it in the picture
No laser line seen. Is the laser on, and set to %1$s?

scan.ply is the point cloud in millimetres, Z up, over the board. The folder as a whole is a session for photogrammetry software.\n\nOn a computer: connect the phone over USB and open Download/EasyScanner.
The scan session was closed and saved to %1$s.
The scan session was closed; copying it to Download failed, it stays in the app (%1$s) and is offered at the next start.
The copy to Download failed (%1$s). The scan stays in the app\'s files: %2$s
Nothing was captured: the scan had no points and no photos.
